hints: At constant speed up the hill, acceleration is zero, so driving force balances resistance and the downslope component of weight.
Multiply the driving force by the constant speed $v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find power $P = F_D \times v$.
walkthrough:
Since the lorry travels up the hill at constant speed ($a = 0$), the driving force $F_D$ must balance the resistance force and the component of weight down the slope:
$$F_D = F_{\text{res}} + mg\sin 3^\circ = 1480 + 7850(10)\sin 3^\circ$$
$$F_D = 1480 + 78500\sin 3^\circ \approx 1480 + 4108.33 \approx 5588.33\text{ N}$$

Calculate the power output of the engine using $P = F_D \times v$ with $v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 5588.33 \times 10 \approx 55883.3\text{ W} \approx 55900\text{ W} = 55.9\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the force balance along the inclined plane for steady motion at constant speed:
$$F_D = F_{\text{res}} + mg\sin\theta$$

Substitute the given mass $m = 7850\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, $\theta = 3^\circ$, and $F_{\text{res}} = 1480\text{ N}$:
$$F_D = 1480 + 7850 \times 10 \times \sin 3^\circ$$
$$F_D = 1480 + 78500\sin 3^\circ$$

Evaluate the weight component and sum the forces:
$$78500\sin 3^\circ \approx 78500 \times 0.0523360 = 4108.374\text{ N}$$
$$F_D = 1480 + 4108.374 = 5588.374\text{ N}$$

Apply the power formula $P = F_D \times v$ with speed $v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 5588.374 \times 10 = 55883.74\text{ W}$$

Round the result to 3 significant figures:
$$P = 55900\text{ W} \text{ (or } 55.9\text{ kW)}$$

hints: The lorry is moving down the hill, so driving force $F_D$ and the component of gravity $mg\sin 3^\circ$ both act down the slope, while resistance $1480\text{ N}$ acts up the slope.
Apply Newton's second law down the slope: $F_D + mg\sin 3^\circ - 1480 = ma$.
Substitute $m = 7850\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $a = 0.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to solve for $F_D$.
Calculate power using $P = F_D \times v$ with $v = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law in the downhill direction of motion:
$$F_D + mg\sin 3^\circ - F_{\text{res}} = ma$$
$$F_D + 7850(10)\sin 3^\circ - 1480 = 7850(0.8)$$

Evaluate each term and solve for the driving force $F_D$:
$$78500\sin 3^\circ \approx 4108.37\text{ N}$$
$$7850(0.8) = 6280\text{ N}$$
$$F_D + 4108.37 - 1480 = 6280$$
$$F_D + 2628.37 = 6280 \implies F_D = 6280 - 2628.37 \approx 3651.63\text{ N}$$

Calculate the engine power at speed $v = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = F_D \times v = 3651.63 \times 15 \approx 54774.45\text{ W} \approx 54800\text{ W} = 54.8\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Set up Newton's second law directed downwards along the inclined road:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma \implies F_D + mg\sin\theta - F_{\text{res}} = ma$$

Substitute $m = 7850\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, $\theta = 3^\circ$, $F_{\text{res}} = 1480\text{ N}$, and $a = 0.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$F_D + 78500\sin 3^\circ - 1480 = 7850 \times 0.8$$

Compute the right-hand side and the gravitational component:
$$7850 \times 0.8 = 6280$$
$$78500\sin 3^\circ \approx 78500 \times 0.0523360 = 4108.374$$
$$F_D + 4108.374 - 1480 = 6280$$
$$F_D + 2628.374 = 6280$$

Subtract $2628.374$ from both sides to find $F_D$:
$$F_D = 6280 - 2628.374 = 3651.626\text{ N}$$

Use the relationship between power, force, and instantaneous velocity:
$$P = F_D \times v = 3651.626 \times 15 = 54774.39\text{ W}$$

State the answer to 3 significant figures:
$$P = 54800\text{ W} \text{ (or } 54.8\text{ kW)}$$
